rules: Never infer Blu-ray or Ultra HD Blu-ray from 1080p/2160p alone.
Resolution and physical source are separate facts and may both be displayed.
REMUX must be confirmed by source metadata or naming, never inferred from resolution.
Dolby Vision/HDR10+/IMAX Enhanced/Atmos/TrueHD/DTS:X are shown only when confirmed.
Prefer one badge per fact in the primary row; retain additional details in the technical text line.
Use dark folder on gray/dark Nuvio themes and light folder on white/light Nuvio themes.
Always replace every provider-owned stream description with the shared Core presentation.
When native StreamBadge rules are active, technical text provides matcher tokens for image badges.
When native StreamBadge rules are inactive, emoji-grouped technical text remains the universal visual fallback.
TMDB may fill media context, runtime and age rating, but never invent stream resolution/source/codec/audio/language facts.
Continuous numeric measurements such as bitrate stay exact in the technical text; static badges identify the normalized measurement class rather than inventing a finite bitrate vocabulary.
Frame-rate and audio sample-rate badges use canonical common values; unknown or unusual numeric values remain visible in technical text without a false badge.
Public language badges use ISO/BCP-47 style language identifiers; legacy provider tokens such as VF, VFF, VFQ, VO and VOSTFR are input aliases only and must never be public badge IDs.
Subtitle badges mirror the same universal language-code model as audio-language badges.
Age-rating badges preserve recognized regional rating systems when explicit and otherwise fall back to universal numeric age badges.

Every material public badge/feed change requires incrementing PUBLIC_FEED_VERSION and publishing new immutable dark/light/transparent/fusion versioned JSON files; previously published versioned feeds remain untouched.
HLS/DASH describe delivery, not visual quality; expose them when the stream URL/type proves the format.
Stream Score is emitted only from proven technical facts plus playback/network evidence; missing playback evidence must not fabricate a global grade.
The compact Stream Score badge uses only S+, S, A+, A, B, C, D or E; the numeric 0-100 score remains in technical detail.
Playback quality is normalized against the media bitrate using throughput headroom, startup time, stalls and segment success; raw network Mbps alone is not a quality grade.
Every published badge catalogue, mapping and versioned feed is immutable. A badge addition/change creates a new vN+1 file; old references remain available for pinned compatibility.
